newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's telecom company to call two big tenders.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's telecom company to call two big tenders.

text.p: Bulgarian Telecommunication Company (BTC), which is preparing for partial privatisation, plans to call tenders for construction of two major optical links by year-end, its chairman said on Friday.
Mihail Danov told a news conference BTC was negotiating with the European Union's Phare programme to help fund the construction of the two optical links.
"We hope to receive some five million Ecus," Danov said.
The links will be between Sofia and the town of Petrich, which is close to the Greek border and between the town of Haskovo and Greece's town of Kavalla on the Aegean Sea.
Danov gave no details of the projected cost of the project.
The World Bank is expected to approve the winner in a BTC tender for the construction of a management information system, Danov said, adding that seven firms had bid for the $10 million project.
Bulgaria and Romania will officially start operating an optical cable link through the only bridge over the Danube River linking the two Balkan countries on December 23, Danov said.
Bulgaria has also completed the construction of its part of an optical link between the town of Svilengrad, which is close to the Turkish border and the town of Odrin in Turkey.
"We hope to put the link in operation within a month," Danov said.
Bulgaria and Yugoslavia launched an optical telephone link in August, boosting trans-Europe communications.
Danov said BTC had completed all but one of its 11 exchanges under its DON (Digital Overlay Network) project.
